text:
maria: launching rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx canary on 8% traffic now. early perf looks good but want eyes on longdoc/citation slice. posting quick snapshot. :mag:

 dmitri: can you paste numbers?

 maria: dashboard: https://console.redwood.example/dash/rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx/canary
```
baseline      p95: 430ms | longdoc_mrr: 0.845 | citation_hallu: 0.8%
canary (8%)   p95: 365ms | longdoc_mrr: 0.837 | citation_hallu: 1.9%
```

 hao: latency win is nice but citation hallucination nearly doubled. is this just long context tokenization edge?

 maria: slice is longdoc_citations, median ctx ~3200 tokens. trace logs show deviations around reference closing brackets.

 lina: could be conditional prob shifts from int4 quant. quick mitigation: (1) drop canary to 1% to limit exposure, (2) enable kv-prefix warmup and deterministic shadow run. also add an auto-fallback rule.

 dmitri: propose auto-fallback criteria: if longdoc_mrr drops by >=1.0% over 5m OR citation_hallu >=1.5% for 3m -> revert to rwd-v3.0-fp16. Also ensure the fallback checks token-level divergence >1.0% before promoting.

 hao: sample auto-fallback config (yaml):
```yaml
auto_fallback:
  - id: longdoc_mrr_guard_v2
    slice: longdoc_citations
    comparator: relative_drop
    threshold_pct: 1.0
    window_seconds: 300
    action: revert_to: rwd-v3.0-fp16
  - id: cite_hallu_guard_v2
    slice: longdoc_citations
    comparator: absolute
    threshold_pct: 1.5
    window_seconds: 180
    action: revert_to: rwd-v3.0-fp16
metrics_for_promotion:
  - token_divergence_pct_threshold: 1.0
```

 maria: doing actions: lowering canary to 1% now, kicking deterministic shadow compare. @canary-bot set-canary rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx 1% --note "reduce after hallu spike"

 canary-bot: Canary update: rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx scaled to 1% (requested by maria)  changes applied to routing.

 dmitri: run a shadow-compare: `/eval run --suite citation_longdoc --model rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx --control rwd-v3.0-fp16 --deterministic --seed 42 --topk 50 --sample 1%` ETA ~10m

 hao: on runtime I'll flip `kv_warmup_prefix: true` for longctx routes and set `kv_warmup_ratio: 0.6`. watching memory.

 lina: adding console alert: rule "longdoc_quality_watch" severity=P1 -> page. putting temporary oncall note.

 maria: eval completed. preliminary results: token divergence concentrated at citation boundaries, divergence 1.4% vs control, 4 examples where citation text was invented.

 dmitri: divergence >1.0% and absolute hallu >1.5% meet our fallback rules. since criteria met, we should revert. manual rollback preferred.

 maria: rolling back now. @canary-bot revert rwd-v3.1-int4-longctx --to rwd-v3.0-fp16 --note "rollback after shadow divergence"

 canary-bot: Revert initiated. Traffic restored to rwd-v3.0-fp16 for affected route. :white_check_mark:

 lina: good. please capture anonymized examples + reproducer steps. owner: maria & hao. include per-layer quant sensitivity as action items.

 hao: will run per-layer sensitivity sweep and an outlier-aware quant pass next week. will report results here.

 maria: created onboarding incident ticket and brief postmortem outline. plan: per-layer sweep -> shadow 0.5% runs -> small-step promotion with token-divergence gating.

 dmitri: update rollout runbook to include these auto-fallback thresholds and token divergence gating. leaving thread for notes.

 maria: thanks all. TL;DR: 8% -> 1% canary after early hallu signal -> deterministic shadow showed divergence -> manual rollback to fp16 -> follow-ups: per-layer quantization experiments + staged shadow runs.
